links.outcome: Clinician diagnostic accuracy with versus without fixed AI advice in paired reader study
links.effect: Accuracy 92.1% with fixed AI advice vs 89.1% without (difference 3.03 percentage points; 95% CI 1.47 to 4.55); 93 incorrect-to-correct and 41 correct-to-incorrect transitions.
links.quote: In the reader study, five clinicians made 1,716 matched reader–case–decision assessments; accuracy was 92.1% with fixed AI advice and 89.1% without advice (difference, 3.03 percentage points; fixed-reader case-bootstrap 95% confidence interval, 1.47 to 4.55), with 93 incorrect-to-correct and 41 correct-to-incorrect transitions.

links.outcome: clinician diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI advice
links.effect: Accuracy was 92.1% with AI advice and 89.1% without; difference 3.03 percentage points, 95% CI 1.47 to 4.55.
links.quote: In the reader study, five clinicians made 1,716 matched reader–case–decision assessments; accuracy was 92.1% with fixed AI advice and 89.1% without advice (difference, 3.03 percentage points; fixed-reader case-bootstrap 95% confidence interval, 1.47 to 4.55), with 93 incorrect-to-correct and 41 correct-to-incorrect transitions.

links.effect: Infection identification improved by 3.63 and 1.48 points; tuberculous-aetiology differences were -5.48 and − 5.40 points.
links.quote: Structured MDT-guided reasoning consistently improved broad infection recognition across models and centres, whereas its benefit did not extend to tuberculous-aetiology differentiation.
